category: completed-row proof and operator trust consistency
title: Proof-deferred completed rows retain healthy and consistent-looking presentation
observed_behavior: A proof-deferred row correctly receives operator_status_state=unverified, but the same row falls through to operator_status=Healthy with guidance that the output is present, receives operator_trust_state=consistent-looking because deferred proof adds no trust flag, and contributes to health_counts.ok because its intentionally blank output_health is defaulted to ok.
expected_invariant: When output-existence proof is deferred, every operator-facing label, trust classification, and aggregate health counter must consistently say unverified or not checked; no presentation may assert presence or count the row as healthy until live proof exists.
root_cause: The deferred-proof state was added to the status-state helper and validation path without being propagated to the older guidance, trust-field, and health-aggregation fallbacks, each of which treats absence of a blocker as affirmative health.
failure_scenario: A summary or bounded Completed Output refresh skips filesystem proof for an older row. The detail state says unverified, while the headline says Healthy, trust says consistent-looking, guidance says the output is present, and dashboard health counts it as ok. An operator can accept, clean up, or promote based on contradictory positive evidence.
evidence: policy_evidence.py lines 142-146 explicitly maps output_exists=None to unverified.
policy_guidance.py lines 209-211 has an unconditional all-clear fallback that does not distinguish None and states that output is present.
trust_fields.py lines 109-116 similarly falls through to consistent-looking when there are no other flags.
policy_orchestration.py lines 240-242 intentionally emits output_exists=None and blank output_health for deferred proof, then lines 382-391 defaults blank health to ok.

test_completed_proof_budget.py lines 113-145 asserts only output_exists, consistency, validation, and operator_status_state; it does not assert the headline label, trust state, guidance, or health count.
affected_flows: Completed Output summary and bounded-proof refresh
completed row detail and operator guidance
final-library eligibility review and cleanup/rerun decisions
existing_safeguards: operator_status_state is unverified for None existence proof.
validation_status_state is validation-needed and consistency_status is Unverified.
Live proof still marks explicit missing output as blocked.
safeguard_gap: The correct low-level state coexists with three affirmative presentation fallbacks, so consumers that render headline, trust, guidance, or health counts can still communicate a false all-clear.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_completed_proof_budget.py covers deferred proof budgeting, no filesystem touch, Unverified consistency, validation-needed, and unverified status state.
tests_missing: Full deferred-row DTO assertion that headline, trust state, guidance, output health, and summary counts are all unverified.
WebView completed-row rendering with contradictory fields rejected or rendered conservatively.
recommended_remediation: Introduce one canonical deferred-proof predicate and apply it before all healthy/default branches. Emit an explicit unverified operator label, trust state, guidance, and health value, and aggregate blank/deferred health separately from ok. Add a full DTO and summary-count regression test.
remediation_risk: low-to-medium: changes operator labels and count buckets but not media policy or filesystem behavior; preserve the distinction among explicit missing, deferred/unverified, and verified-present output
validation_rung: Focused completed proof-budget, policy, facade, and WebView rendering tests plus generated-contract checks; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Follow-on to the untraceable LOW-1 test comment at test_completed_proof_budget.py lines 133-134: status-state handling was corrected, but the broader headline/trust/aggregate presentation remains inconsistent. AUDIT-FIND-W05-002 separately covers boolean false collapsing inside subtitle QA.

title: Final-library promotion active-run evidence is write-only and non-gating

locations.symbol: FinalLibraryPromotionServiceMixin state initialization and active writer

observed_behavior: The service initializes active state to None and has no reader for active_run.json anywhere in source. Active-state write failures are caught and logged, yet the non-daemon mutation worker starts anyway. Conversely, the terminal write_run_manifest call in finally is not guarded; if it raises, the subsequent in-memory clear and active-file deletion do not execute.
expected_invariant: A high-risk promotion run must not start without durable lifecycle intent, terminalization must clear or transition activity even when evidence persistence fails, and startup/status must reconcile a durable in-progress record rather than silently treating it as nonexistent.
root_cause: In-memory state is treated as the operational authority while active_run.json is a best-effort write-only mirror, and start/finalization use opposite but both unsafe failure policies: ignore the initial write error, then allow the terminal write error to skip cleanup.
failure_scenario: A permission, disk-full, or transient filesystem error prevents the initial active write and promotion still moves files with no durable active evidence. A backend crash then leaves no recoverable activity state. Separately, a terminal run-manifest write failure exits the worker before clearing _final_library_promotion_active, leaving close-readiness and future starts blocked by a run whose thread has already ended.
evidence: service.py lines 27-32 always initializes missing in-memory active state to None.
service.py lines 64-70 suppresses every write_active_run exception.
service.py lines 193-220 creates activity, invokes the suppressing writer, and starts the thread without checking durable success.
promotion.py lines 296-303 only writes or deletes active_run.json; a source-wide search found no active-run reader.
service.py lines 344-352 calls write_run_manifest before the lock/clear block, so an exception skips both in-memory and durable active cleanup.
test_final_library_promotion.py lines 1230-1332 covers duplicate in-memory starts, non-daemon workers, and close blocking only on successful state writes/finalization.
affected_flows: final-library promotion start, status, pause, and close-readiness
durable promotion recovery after backend interruption
future promotion launch after a worker-finalization error
existing_safeguards: Only one in-memory active run is accepted per service instance.
The worker is non-daemon and close-readiness reports live in-memory activity.
Per-item transfer has its own staging, verification, and rollback controls.
Active write failures are logged.
safeguard_gap: Those safeguards neither make lifecycle intent durable before mutation nor reconcile stale/missing activity after restart, and an evidence-write error can itself strand the in-memory guard.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_final_library_promotion.py covers normal selected promotion, duplicate live start rejection, non-daemon close blocking, and normal terminal evidence.
tests_missing: Initial active-run write failure prevents worker start.
Terminal run-manifest write failure still transitions/clears activity and exposes an actionable error.
Service restart reloads and reconciles active_run.json plus incomplete transaction artifacts.
Close-readiness behavior after evidence persistence failure.
recommended_remediation: Make durable active intent a checked prerequisite to thread start. Add a reader and explicit startup reconciliation state for active_run.json. Restructure worker finalization so activity always reaches a terminal in-memory/durable state even when run-manifest persistence fails, retaining the persistence failure as operator-visible evidence rather than swallowing or stranding it.
remediation_risk: high: this changes lifecycle authority around filesystem mutation and must preserve non-daemon shutdown, one-run exclusion, per-item rollback, and recovery from legacy stale active files
validation_rung: Focused final-library service fault-injection tests for active/run-manifest writes, restart reconciliation, pause/close readiness, and synthetic transactional promotion fixtures; representative real-media validation is advisable before release if transfer behavior is changed.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding record matched the write-only active state or asymmetric lifecycle-write failure policy.

title: Second-resolution promotion run IDs can overwrite durable run evidence
observed_behavior: Run identity is derived only from utc_now_text(), which truncates to whole seconds. Two sequential runs that both start within the same UTC second receive the same run_id, and their run and per-row item manifests resolve to identical filenames that are atomically replaced rather than uniquely created.
expected_invariant: Every promotion command must receive a collision-resistant immutable run identity so durable run/item evidence from one accepted mutation can never be overwritten by another.
root_cause: A display timestamp with one-second precision is reused as the persistence key without a UUID, monotonic suffix, exclusive-create check, or collision retry.
failure_scenario: A fast selected-item run completes and another is started before the clock advances. The second run overwrites the first run's .run.json and any same-row .item.json, while responses and item evidence carry the indistinguishable run_id. Audit and recovery can no longer prove which command produced which promotion result.
evidence: results.py lines 8-9 formats UTC with timespec=seconds.
service.py line 183 creates run_id solely by punctuation replacement on that value.
promotion.py lines 306-317 deterministically names run and item manifests from run_id and row-key hash, then uses atomic replacement without collision rejection.
The service tests exercise one run at a time or hold the first run active; none starts two completed runs inside one second or asserts distinct durable paths.
existing_safeguards: An in-memory guard prevents overlapping active runs.
Manifest replacement is atomic, preventing torn JSON.
Row-key hashing separates different items within a run.
safeguard_gap: The guard permits immediately sequential runs, atomic replacement safely destroys the earlier evidence, and row-key hashing cannot distinguish the same row across colliding runs.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_final_library_promotion.py covers normal single-run evidence and concurrent active-run rejection.
tests_missing: Two sequential runs under a frozen same-second clock receive distinct IDs and preserve both run/item manifests.
Exclusive collision handling for a preexisting run ID.
recommended_remediation: Generate run IDs with a UUID or cryptographically random suffix, or at minimum microsecond precision plus exclusive-create collision handling. Keep human time in a separate field and add same-clock deterministic regression tests that prove both evidence sets remain present.
remediation_risk: low-to-medium: run IDs are externally returned and embedded in filenames/item evidence, so consumers and retention tooling must accept the new shape without losing old manifests
validation_rung: Focused final-library service/persistence tests with a frozen clock and repeated same-row runs, plus API/WebView evidence-correlation checks; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding record matched this run-identity collision root cause.

title: Rename undo cannot recover after a mid-sequence mutation failure
observed_behavior: Undo preflights the original all-forward state, writes undoing, then reverses operations one by one without a completed-operation checkpoint or compensation. If a later rename fails, the catch records only failed status. A retry re-runs the all-forward preflight, sees the destinations of already-restored operations as missing, and refuses to continue.
expected_invariant: A multi-path rename undo must be atomic or durably resumable: after any interruption, the manifest must identify each committed reversal and support safe continuation or compensation without requiring manual path reconstruction.
root_cause: The undo manifest stores only one run-level status and error list. The mutation loop has no per-operation journal, staged two-phase plan, rollback of completed reversals, or recovery-aware preflight for a partially undone layout.
failure_scenario: A media/sidecar rename set begins undo, restores one or more paths, then encounters a sharing violation, disconnect, collision, or metadata write failure. The manifest becomes failed while the library is partially renamed. Retrying reports renamed path is missing for every already-restored item, so the strict backend workflow cannot complete or roll back the set.
evidence: undo_runner.py lines 104-107 requires every current destination to exist and every original target to be absent before mutation.
undo_runner.py lines 222-225 persists only run-level undoing state.
undo_runner.py lines 229-258 performs irreversible per-path renames in sequence without checkpoint or compensation.
undo_runner.py lines 267-272 records one failed status/error and rethrows, leaving earlier successful operations in place.

test_service_rename_apply_runner.py lines 149-184 covers successful multi-operation undo and lines 186-249 cover failures detected before mutation; there is no injected mid-loop failure and retry test.
affected_flows: rename apply undo for media and sidecars
existing_safeguards: Manifest/root path boundaries and collision checks run before mutation.
Operations execute in reverse order.
Undo start/failure/completion states and error text are persisted.
Already-completed undo is rejected.
safeguard_gap: Preflight protects only the initial layout. Once any rename succeeds, there is no durable operation-level state or compensation, and the same preflight makes the failed transaction non-resumable.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_rename_apply_runner.py covers successful multi-path undo, missing destination preflight rejection, and unsafe metadata-backup rejection before mutation.
tests_missing: Injected failure after the first of multiple undo operations.
Retry/resume from a partially undone manifest.
Compensation failure with durable per-operation evidence.
Interruption between a filesystem rename and its checkpoint.
recommended_remediation: Journal each undo operation with prepared/committed state using atomic manifest writes, make preflight recognize the exact mixed layout described by that journal, and resume committed progress safely. Alternatively compensate already-reversed operations before returning failure, with durable evidence for compensation failures. Add deterministic fault injection at every operation boundary.
remediation_risk: high: rename apply/undo mutates media and sidecar paths; recovery must preserve path boundaries, case-only behavior, collision guarantees, metadata backups, and source-content immutability
validation_rung: Focused rename undo transaction/fault-injection tests across media, sidecar, case-only, collision, metadata, and restart boundaries; representative synthetic filesystem validation is required, while real-media decoding is not.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from CSW-2026-07-09-RENAME-004, which covers frontend history re-enabling an already completed undo; this finding covers backend partial-mutation recovery before completion.

title: Pending-publish locking is per manifest rather than per destination

locations.symbol: Invoke-PendingDrainTransactionCore destination check and partial copy

observed_behavior: Each drain acquires only ManifestPath.lock. Separate manifests that name the same server_out can therefore drain concurrently in separate PowerShell processes. Both can pass the destination-absent check and copy transaction-specific partials; reveal then moves the first and replaces it with the second. Each transaction's post-reveal hash/rollback logic can inspect or remove bytes written by the other. Python reports duplicate targets as health text but explicitly does not change drain behavior.
expected_invariant: All checks, sidecar staging, atomic reveal, verification, rollback, completion evidence, and pending cleanup for one canonical final destination must be serialized under a destination-scoped cross-process lock; duplicate-target manifests must fail closed until reconciled.
root_cause: The transaction mutex key is the manifest filename, while the shared mutable resource is canonical server_out plus its sidecars. Duplicate-target detection exists only in the Python read model and is not an enforced PowerShell drain precondition.
failure_scenario: Two pending manifests with different payloads target the same absent final path and two drains overlap. One reveals, the other replaces it and records a backup. The first can then hash the second payload as a mismatch and remove the shared final because its own reveal had no backup; the second can subsequently restore or verify stale bytes. Final media, sidecars, completion rows, and both manifests can disagree even though each per-manifest lock behaved correctly.
evidence: pending_transactions.ps1 lines 74-89 derives the exclusive lock only from ManifestPath.
pending_drain_transaction.ps1 lines 133-152 acquires that manifest lock and no destination lock.
pending_drain_transaction.ps1 lines 214-315 checks destination existence before a long copy-to-partial window.
publish_partial.ps1 lines 166-175 replaces a destination that appeared after the earlier check; lines 185-205 can remove the current final when verification fails and the caller has no backup.
pending_push.ps1 lines 469-470 enumerates manifests and lines 559-598 dispatches each independently, with no global/destination lock visible.
pending_service.py lines 253-269 documents that duplicate target marking does not change drain behavior; test_pending_publish_service.py lines 219-242 asserts diagnostics only.
The requested static-only audit prohibited the disposable concurrent-process reproduction, so the exact interleaving remains intentionally unexecuted.
affected_flows: duplicate strict drain delivery across processes
repair/reconcile outputs that introduce duplicate server destinations
existing_safeguards: A per-manifest FileShare.None lock blocks duplicate handling of the same manifest.
Transaction-specific partial paths, hashes, sidecar backups, and reveal backups support single-transaction recovery.
Existing destinations are collision-checked when visible before the copy window.
Python surfaces duplicate local/destination targets as health rows.
safeguard_gap: None of the safeguards serializes two different manifests on the same final identity, and the diagnostic duplicate state is not consulted by the drain engine. Single-transaction rollback can mutate the other transaction's committed result.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-PendingPublishTransactionFaultInjectionChecks.ps1 covers single-transaction fault boundaries and completion evidence.
tests_missing: Two separate PowerShell processes draining different manifests to one server_out.
Destination lock canonicalization across case and separator aliases.
Concurrent sidecar backup/reveal and final-hash rollback ordering.
Fail-closed drain behavior when the pending index reports duplicate targets.
recommended_remediation: Acquire a cross-process lock keyed by a canonical destination identity before the existence check and hold it through media/sidecar reveal, verification, completion evidence, and cleanup. Re-read manifest and destination state after locking. Treat duplicate server_out manifests as a reconcile-required state rather than merely diagnostic, and retain the per-manifest lock for same-manifest idempotency.
remediation_risk: high: lock canonicalization and ordering can deadlock or split identities across aliases; preserve manifest locking, source/scratch isolation, no-overwrite collision policy, sidecar rollback, and recovery after process termination
validation_rung: Static checks plus a disposable two-process synthetic race harness with exact before/after hashes, sidecars, manifests, and completion rows; pending safety/fault-injection and repair/drain suites; representative real-media park/drain validation is required before release because final-placement policy changes.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding record matched the destination-scoped lock gap. AUDIT-FIND-W01-001 makes duplicate strict delivery possible at the HTTP layer, while AUDIT-FIND-W15-001 covers a separate repair/drain contract mismatch.

title: Completed-manifest duplicate suppression occurs outside the append lock
observed_behavior: Add-CompletedJobsManifestEntry scans completed_jobs.jsonl for the transaction/hash before calling Write-JsonLineAppend with the cross-process lock. Two processes can both complete the unlocked absence check, then serialize two identical appends under the lock. The lock prevents torn lines but does not make check-and-append idempotent.
expected_invariant: Completion evidence append must atomically enforce at most one row per completion transaction/hash across concurrent delivery, retry, and process boundaries.
root_cause: Duplicate detection and mutation are split across two lock scopes: the read occurs before the append helper acquires its mutex, and the append helper has no compare-and-append transaction.
failure_scenario: An immediate publish and a pending retry, or two duplicate drain commands, attempt to record the same completed transaction concurrently. Both see no row, both append successfully, and Completed Output, SQLite mirroring, metrics, or maintenance consumers receive duplicate history for one publication.
evidence: sidecar.ps1 lines 266-302 performs the complete duplicate scan without acquiring the append mutex.
sidecar.ps1 lines 315-320 calls that scan before constructing the entry.
sidecar.ps1 line 338 acquires UseLogLock only inside Write-JsonLineAppend after the check has completed.

Invoke-LoggingJsonLineChecks.ps1 covers concurrent append integrity and row preservation, while pending fault injection covers sequential ambiguous-response idempotency; neither holds the race window with identical transaction IDs.
affected_flows: immediate and pending publish completion evidence
ambiguous-response retries and duplicate command delivery
existing_safeguards: Sequential/restart retries find an existing transaction/hash and return success without appending.
The JSONL append mutex prevents interleaved or torn writes.
Completed-row consumers retain transaction/hash fields for diagnosis.
safeguard_gap: Serialization of writes is not atomic with the uniqueness predicate, so the exact concurrent case bypasses sequential idempotency while still producing valid JSONL lines.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-PendingPublishTransactionFaultInjectionChecks.ps1 covers completion append failures and single-transaction recovery.
tests_missing: Two processes performing identical Test-then-Append under a controlled barrier.
Assertion that one transaction/hash yields exactly one completed row after concurrent retry.
Consumer behavior when legacy duplicate completion rows exist.
recommended_remediation: Move duplicate lookup and append under one cross-process critical section, or use a transactional keyed store/side index with an atomic uniqueness constraint. Avoid recursively reacquiring the current append mutex; expose a helper that locks once, re-reads under lock, and appends only if absent.
remediation_risk: medium: changing shared logging locks can deadlock or reduce append throughput; preserve crash-safe JSONL writes and compatibility with existing completion history
validation_rung: Controlled two-process JSONL idempotency test, existing logging and pending fault-injection suites, and completed-row mirror/metrics dedup checks; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding record matched this check-then-append lock gap; it is distinct from destination reveal serialization and from the generic HTTP replay defect.
